corrected_value.authors: O’Donnell, M., Critcher, C. R., & Nelson, L. D.
corrected_value.title: Bundle Selection and Variety Seeking: The Importance of Combinatorics.

decisions.quote: To clarify the direction of effect, we conducted four studies in two product categories and found evidence of a stronger preference for variety in bundled offering conditions (compared to single offering conditions), replicating O’Donnell et al.’s (2023) findings.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are absent for this never-adjudicated work. Across the Abstract, Introduction, Study 1a Method, Results, and General Discussion, Pfeifer and Schreiner (2024/2025) explicitly re-test the reversed offer framing effect reported by O'Donnell, Critcher, and Nelson (2023, Supplemental Study E) across four experiments (Studies 1a, 1b, 2a, and 2b) using O'Donnell et al.'s modified choice instructions, comparing variety-seeking proportions between bundled and single offering conditions against O'Donnell et al.'s (2023) empirical findings. The reference list (lines 430–434) and Crossref metadata verify the identity: O’Donnell, M., Critcher, C. R., & Nelson, L. D. (2023), 'Bundle Selection and Variety Seeking: The Importance of Combinatorics,' The Journal of Consumer Research, 49(5), 861–881, DOI 10.1093/jcr/ucac017. The sole shipped row 1209 is Mittelman, Andrade, Chattopadhyay, & Brendl (2014, 'The Offer Framing Effect: Choosing Single versus Bundled Offerings Affects Variety Seeking', 10.1086/678193), which is the earlier conflicting study by different authors that O'Donnell et al. (2023) contradicted; thus report equivalence does not apply and O'Donnell et al. (2023) is a genuinely absent original.
